Document 1795: Report: Model X In Latest Tesla Autopilot Death Accelerated And Steered Into Barrier
The National Transportation Safety Board has issued a [preliminary report on the Tesla Model X P100D crash that killed its occupant](https://www.ntsb.gov/investigations/AccidentReports/Reports/HWY18FH011-preliminary.pdf) on March 23rd on a highway in California. The report has detailed information on the pre-crash events. Part of the information retrieved from the Tesla data logged by the vehicle shows that the Tesla accelerated just prior to the impact to speeds above the posted speed limit and that the car seems to have steered itself directly into the barrier.
美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）已发布了一份关于3月23日发生在加利福尼亚州高速公路上致车内乘员死亡的特斯拉Model X P100D车祸的初步报告。该报告包含了关于撞车前事件的详细信息。从车辆记录的特斯拉数据中检索到的部分信息显示，特斯拉在撞击前加速至超过标示限速，且车辆似乎自行直接转向撞向了隔离栏。
Included in the report is the statement "At 3 seconds prior to the crash and up to the time of impact with the crash attenuator,the Tesla’s speed increased from 62 to 70.8 mph, with no precrash braking or evasive steering movement detected." The speed limit on that roadway is 65 MPH. The report also says that the Autopilot system was set by the driver to 10 MPH higher than the speed limit. Prior to the car accelerating, it had been following another car (using adaptive cruise control) and thus, was traveling slower than the setpoint of the Autopilot.
Lane-keeping assist was engaged leading up to the moment of the crash. The Model X had been following another vehicle that did not crash, but steered itself out of the lane and into the barrier.
报告中包含如下陈述：“在撞车前3秒直至撞击防撞桶的时刻，特斯拉的速度从62英里/小时增加到了70.8英里/小时，未检测到撞车前制动或规避转向操作。”该路段的限速为65英里/小时。报告还指出，驾驶员将Autopilot系统的设定速度调至比限速高出10英里/小时。在车辆加速之前，它一直跟随另一辆车（使用自适应巡航控制），因此行驶速度低于Autopilot的设定值。
Although the car was engulfed in flames when the vehicle's lithium batteries caught fire, the driver was pulled free by bystanders who found him in his seat with seatbelt on. The fire department required hundreds of gallons of fire foam and ten minutes to extinguish the flames.
Five days after the crash, the battery re-ignited.
车道保持辅助系统在撞车前一直处于开启状态。这辆Model X此前一直跟随另一辆未发生事故的车辆，但却自行驶出车道并撞向了隔离栏。
As we have previously reported, [an NTSB report on an earlier crash of Tesla Model S using Autopilot seemed to eerily predict more crashes](https://www.torquenews.com/1083/ntsb-report-eerily-predicts-tesla-model-x-autopilot-fatality-6-months-advance). According to that report, "The way in which the Tesla “Autopilot” system monitored and responded to the driver’s interaction with the steering wheel was not an effective method of ensuring driver engagement.风险源" In this crash, the report says the data indicate, "During the 60 seconds prior to the crash, the driver’s hands were detected on the steering wheel on three separate occasions, for a total of 34 seconds; for the last 6 seconds prior to the crash, the vehicle did not detect the driver’s hands on the steering wheel."
Document 189: Tesla in fatal California crash was on Autopilot
**Electric carmaker Tesla says a vehicle involved in a fatal crash in California was in Autopilot mode, raising further questions about the safety of self-driving technology.**
电动汽车制造商特斯拉表示，在加利福尼亚州发生的一起致命车祸中，肇事车辆正处于“自动辅助驾驶”（Autopilot）模式，这引发了人们对自动驾驶技术安全性的进一步质疑。
One of the company's Model X cars crashed into a roadside barrier and caught fire on 23 March.
Tesla says Autopilot was engaged at the time of the accident involving the driver, 38, who died soon afterwards.
该公司的一辆Model X汽车于3月23日撞上路边护栏并起火。
But they did not say whether the system had detected the concrete barrier.
"The driver had received several visual and one audible hands-on warning earlier in the drive," [a statement on the company's website](https://www.tesla.com/blog/update-last-week%E2%80%99s-accident) said.
特斯拉称，事故发生时自动辅助驾驶系统处于开启状态，涉事司机年仅38岁，随后不久不幸身亡。
"The driver's hands were not detected on the wheel for six seconds prior to the collision."
"The driver had about five seconds and 150m (490ft) of unobstructed view of the concrete divider... but the vehicle logs show that no action was taken," the statement added.
但该公司并未说明该系统当时是否检测到了混凝土护栏。
Tesla's Autopilot system does some of the things a fully autonomous machine can do. It can brake, accelerate and steer by itself under certain conditions, but it is classified as a driver assistance system, is not intended to operate independently and as such the driver is meant to have their hands on the wheel at all times.
In 2016, [a Tesla driver was killed in Florida](http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-36680043) when his car failed to spot a lorry crossing its path.
“在此前的行驶过程中，司机已收到数次视觉提醒和一次听觉提醒，提示其将双手放在方向盘上，”公司网站上的一份声明写道。
It led the company to introduce new safety measures, including turning off Autopilot and bringing the car to a halt if the driver lets go of the wheel for too long.
The accident in California comes at a difficult time for self-driving technology.
“在碰撞发生前的六秒钟内，系统未检测到司机的双手在方向盘上。”
Earlier this month, Uber was forbidden from resuming self-driving tests in the US state of Arizona.
It followed [a fatal crash in the state](http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43497364) in which an autonomous vehicle hit a woman who was walking her bike across the road.
声明补充道：“司机大约有五秒钟的时间和150米（490英尺）的无遮挡视野可以看到混凝土隔离带……但车辆日志显示司机未采取任何行动。”
It was thought to be the first time an autonomous car had been involved in a fatal collision with a pedestrian.
The company suspended all self-driving tests in North America after the accident.
特斯拉的自动辅助驾驶系统具备全自动驾驶机器的部分功能。它可以在特定条件下自动刹车、加速和转向，但被归类为驾驶辅助系统，并非旨在独立运行，因此要求司机始终将双手放在方向盘上。
Document 192: Family of Tesla driver killed in Model X crash on Autopilot is preparing to sue Tesla
The safety of Tesla Autopilot came back into focus after it was confirmed that the driver assist system was on during the fatal accident that killed a Model X owner in Mountain View last month.
在上月山景城一名Model X车主因致命事故身亡后，确认事发时驾驶辅助系统处于开启状态，特斯拉Autopilot的安全性再次成为焦点。
Now the family of the deceased say that they are prepared to sue Tesla after a media interview.
As we previously reported, the Model X was driving on Autopilot when it entered the median of a ramp on the highway as if it was a lane and hit a barrier about a hundred and fifty meters after going into the median.
如今，逝者家属在接受媒体采访后表示，他们准备起诉特斯拉。
The impact was quite severe because there was no crash attenuator since it was already destroyed from a previous crash. The driver was rushed to the hospital, but he, unfortunately, died of his injuries.
Sevonne Huang, the wife of the driver, Walter Huang, gave an interview to ABC7 yesterday.受影响方
据我们此前报道，这辆Model X在Autopilot开启状态下行驶时，驶入了高速公路匝道的中间隔离带，仿佛将其当作一条车道，并在进入隔离带约一百五十米后撞上了隔离带内的护栏。
During the interview, she said that her husband had previously complained about the Autopilot’s behaviour at hat exact location:
Sevonne Huang: “And he want to show me, but a lot of time it doesn’t happen.” Dan Noyes: “He told you that the car would drive to that same barrier?” Sevonne: “Yes.” Noyes: “The same barrier that he finally hit?” Sevonne: “Yeah, that’s why I saw the news. I knew that’s him.”
撞击十分猛烈，因为该处没有防撞缓冲设施，此前的一次事故已将其损毁。驾驶员被紧急送往医院，但不幸因伤势过重身亡。
The family hired attorney Mark Fong and say that they are prepared to sue Tesla.
Fong commented:
驾驶员沃尔特·黄（Walter Huang）的妻子Sevonne Huang昨天接受了ABC7的采访。
“Unfortunately, it appears that Tesla has tried to blame the victim here. It took him out of the lane that he was driving in, then it failed to break, then it drove him into this fixed concrete barrier. We believe this would’ve never happened had this Autopilot never been turned on.”
Tesla responded to the interview in a statement:
在采访中，她提到丈夫此前曾抱怨过Autopilot在那个具体位置的行为：
“We are very sorry for the family’s loss. According to the family, Mr. Huang was well aware that Autopilot was not perfect and, specifically, he told them it was not reliable in that exact location, yet he nonetheless engaged Autopilot at that location. The crash happened on a clear day with several hundred feet of visibility ahead, which means that the only way for this accident to have occurred is if Mr. Huang was not paying attention to the road, despite the car providing multiple warnings to do so. The fundamental premise of both moral and legal liability is a broken promise, and there was none here. Tesla is extremely clear that Autopilot requires the driver to be alert and have hands on the wheel. This reminder is made every single time Autopilot is engaged. If the system detects that hands are not on, it provides visual and auditory alerts. This happened several times on Mr. Huang’s drive that day. We empathize with Mr. Huang’s family, who are understandably facing loss and grief, but the false impression that Autopilot is unsafe will cause harm to others on the road. NHTSA found that even the early version of Tesla Autopilot resulted in 40% fewer crashes and it has improved substantially since then.风险控制 The reason that other families are not on TV is because their loved ones are still alive.”
Electrek’s Take
Sevonne Huang：“他想展示给我看，但很多时候它并没有发生。”
I can’t blame the family for having this reaction or any kind of reaction after such a tragic loss, but when it comes to the lawsuit, it looks like they are destroying their own case.
Dan Noyes：“他告诉你，车会开向那个同样的护栏？”
As Tesla said in the statement and as it was confirmed by other Tesla owners recreating the circumstances of the crash, an attentive driver would have plenty of time to go back to the correct lane after the car enters the median, which means that Huang was most likely not paying attention.
Sevonne：“是的。”
On top of it, his wife says that he was aware that Autopilot had difficulties handling this specific situation and yet he decided to activate it anyway and apparently not pay close attention.
Noyes：“就是他最终撞上的那个护栏？”
In my opinion, as long as Tesla is being clear about drivers needing to stay attentive and keep their hands on the steering wheel, there’s not much of a case here that Tesla is responsible for the accident.
Sevonne：“对，所以我看到新闻时。我就知道那是他。”
But with this said, as Tesla Autopilot improves it seems that some drivers are growing more confident with the driver assist system and are putting too much trust in it.
I think it’s important to remind everyone that as long as Tesla doesn’t claim it’s anything more than a level 2 driving system and it’s not thoroughly tested to be anything more than that, they should always stay vigilant and be ready to take control.
家属聘请了律师Mark Fong，并表示准备起诉特斯拉。
Subscribe to Electrek on YouTube for exclusive videos and subscribe the podcast.

Document 271: Google's self-driving Lexus cuts off self-driving Audi
Updated 12:15 a.m ET Friday.
更新于东部时间周五凌晨12:15。
Somebody almost had to call a self-driving tow truck.
Two autonomous vehicles, one powered by Google and the other from Delphi Automotive, nearly collided this week in what’s thought to be the first close call between a pair of self-driving cars, Reuters reports.
差点就得叫一辆自动驾驶拖车了。
The Google car, a modified Lexus, cut off Delphi’s modified Audi and forced it abort changing lanes to avoid a crash, Delphi’s John Absmeier told Reuters. Absmeier was a passenger in the Audi at the time of the incident; nobody was hurt in the event.受影响方
Delphi has two driverless Audi prototypes on California roads, while Google has 20 being tested.
据路透社报道，两辆自动驾驶汽车——一辆由谷歌提供技术支持，另一辆来自德尔福汽车公司——本周险些相撞，这被认为是首起两辆自动驾驶汽车之间的险情。
The near collision raises important questions about self-driving cars, including who’s responsible when two are involved in an accident.
Update: A Delphi spokesperson emailed Fortune with the following statement: “During a demo drive of our automated vehicle, our expert used the interaction with the Google car as an example of the types of scenarios that the car can encounter in real-world driving. It was an anecdote of an interaction, not a ‘near miss’. Reuters completely misrepresented the facts.”
德尔福的约翰·阿布施迈尔告诉路透社，谷歌那辆改装雷克萨斯切入了德尔福改装奥迪的前方，迫使后者为了避让而中止变道。事发时阿布施迈尔正乘坐在这辆奥迪车上；事件中无人受伤。
Document 273: Near-miss between self-driving cars shows computers are smarter than us
[Update 6/27]: In a statement from Delphi, the company has added further clarification and now claims that the two vehicles were never in any danger of colliding. The statement claims the original report from Reuters was incorrect, though the news agency has said it stands by its original report.
[6月27日更新]：德尔福在一份声明中进一步澄清，现声称两辆车从未发生碰撞危险。该声明称路透社最初的报道有误，尽管该新闻机构表示坚持其最初的报道。
The most futuristic car crash in the history of humanity almost took place in Palo Alto, California, this week, when one of Google’s self-driving cars cut off another automated vehicle on a city street. Both cars were under the control of their respective computers, and they didn’t actually collide, but the close call marks a first as driverless vehicles increasingly expand beyond their limited test zones.
John Absmeier, the global business director for Delphi Automotive, was a passenger in his company’s automated vehicle prototype, a driverless Audi Q5, when it encountered one of Google’s self-driving Lexus SUVs.
本周，人类历史上最具未来感的车祸险些在加利福尼亚州帕洛阿尔托发生，当时谷歌的一辆自动驾驶汽车在城市街道上截断了另一辆自动化车辆的去路。两辆车均由各自的电脑控制，虽然并未真正发生碰撞，但随着无人驾驶车辆日益突破其有限的测试区域，这一险情标志着此类事件的首例。
Absmeier told Reuters that his vehicle was negotiating a lane change when the Google vehicle cut it off, causing the Audi to take “appropriate action” to avoid a crash.
The fact that no collision occurred is perhaps the most important takeaway from the story. Self-driving cars are appealing because of both convenience and safety.风险控制 In this situation, two driverless vehicles running two different automated driving programs encountered each other in a potentially dangerous situation风险源—one in which a human driver might have panicked—and both vehicles emerged unscathed.
德尔福汽车公司的全球业务总监约翰·阿布施米尔当时正乘坐其公司的自动化车辆原型——一辆无人驾驶的奥迪Q5，此时它遇到了谷歌的一辆自动驾驶雷克萨斯SUV。
Delphi’s driverless Audi
Delphi Automotive
阿布施米尔告诉路透社，当谷歌车辆截断其去路时，他的车辆正在进行变道，导致奥迪采取了“适当行动”以避免碰撞。
Photo via Delphi Automotive

Document 3156: UnitedHealth Faces Lawsuit, Media Scrutiny Over AI’s Role in Medicare Advantage Denials of Nursing Home Care
UnitedHealthcare, a unit of UnitedHealth Group (NYSE: UNH), is facing a federal lawsuit over its use of an artificial intelligence tool in making Medicare Advantage claims denials for patients in extended care facilities.
联合健康集团（纽交所代码：UNH）旗下的联合健康保险公司正面临一项联邦诉讼，指控其在针对长期护理机构患者的联邦医疗保险优势计划理赔拒赔中使用了人工智能工具。
That same issue was at the center of a [recently published](https://www.statnews.com/2023/11/14/unitedhealth-algorithm-medicare-advantage-investigation/) piece in STAT, a health-oriented news outlet.
Aaron Albright, a spokesperson for Optum, the unit of UnitedHealth involved in the lawsuit’s claims, told Skilled Nursing News that the AI tool used in assessing claims is more for guidance and not for denial of insurance claims.
这一相同问题也是健康类新闻媒体STAT近日发表的一篇文章的核心。
“The \\[NaviHealth\\] predict tool is not used to make coverage determinations. The tool is used as a guide to help us inform providers, families and other caregivers about what sort of assistance and care the patient may need both in the facility and after returning home,” said Albright, via an emailed statement. “Coverage decisions are based on CMS coverage criteria and the terms of the member’s plan. This lawsuit has no merit, and we will defend ourselves vigorously.”
The high level of denials were generated because UnitedHealth’s AI tool – one developed by its subsidiary NaviHealth – does not use input from doctors to predict the length of stay for patients in long-term care, according to the Class Action Complaint.受影响方 Instead, the tool compares a patient’s demographic and medical information against a database of other similar patients, and uses that information to determine how many days United Healthcare will approve a necessary stay at a care facility, the plaintiffs’ lawyers said in a press release. This often “undercuts the amount of time recommended by a physician,” they argue.
联合健康集团涉入诉讼指控的业务部门Optum的发言人Aaron Albright向《专业护理新闻》表示，用于评估理赔的AI工具更多是起指导作用，并非用于拒绝保险理赔。
Upon appeal, the MA denials don’t not hold up once doctors and medical experts review the claims, the lawsuit alleges. In fact, claims denials were reversed in 90% of the cases. That said, the lawyers note that currently, only around 0.2% of patients submit their claims for appeals, with the majority of residents having to pay out of pocket for the rest of their stay at a care facility.
The lawsuit comes after nursing home [providers](https://skillednursingnews.com/2023/08/painful-and-getting-worse-rise-of-medicare-advantage-drains-vast-revenue-from-snf-sector-worsens-workforce-instability/) and [lawmakers](https://skillednursingnews.com/2023/07/astronomical-medicare-advantage-denials-pre-auth-issues-cause-outcry-from-nursing-homes/) have expressed frustration over Medicare Advantage denials by not just UnitedHealth, but other large insurance companies as well.
Albright通过电子邮件声明表示：“[NaviHealth]预测工具并非用于做出承保决定。该工具仅作为指引，帮助我们告知医疗服务提供者、家属及其他护理人员，患者在机构内及返家后可能需要何种援助和护理。承保决定是基于联邦医疗保险和医疗补助服务中心（CMS）的承保标准以及会员计划的条款做出的。此诉讼毫无根据，我们将坚决为自己辩护。”
And the STAT article points out that NaviHealth is used by other large insurance companies as well. “NaviHealth doesn’t just manage nursing home care within UnitedHealth’s plans, but also serves large Medicare Advantage insurers such as Humana and many regional health plans — potentially affecting the care of more than 15 million people, or half of all Medicare Advantage enrollees,” the article states.
NaviHealth set a target for 2023 to keep rehab stays of patients in MA plans within 1% of the days projected by the algorithm, STAT reported, citing internal documents that the publication obtained. The lawsuit seeks to stop UnitedHealth’s use of AI to replace doctor’s orders as well as get restitution for emotional distress damages, compensatory damages and punitive damages, the law firm’s press release stated.
根据集体诉讼投诉书，之所以出现高比例的拒赔，是因为联合健康的AI工具——由其子公司NaviHealth开发——在预测长期护理患者的住院时长时，并未采用医生的输入信息。原告律师在新闻稿中指出，相反，该工具将患者的人口统计和医疗信息与其他类似患者的数据库进行比对，并利用这些信息来决定联合健康保险公司将批准多少天的必要护理机构住院时间。他们认为，这往往“缩短了医生建议的时间”。
Document 3158: America's Largest Health Insurer Denying Care With AI That's Wrong 90 Percent of the Time, Lawsuit Alleges
UnitedHealthcare, the largest health insurance provider in the US, is using an AI algorithm called nH Predict whose wildly inaccurate predictions are being used to deny health coverage to severely ill patients by cutting the time they can spend in extended care, a [new lawsuit alleges](https://cdn.arstechnica.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/class-action-v-unitedhealth-and-navihealth-1.pdf).
一项新的诉讼指控，美国最大的健康保险提供商联合健康保险（UnitedHealthcare）正在使用一种名为 nH Predict 的 AI 算法，其极不准确的预测正被用于剥夺重病患者的保险覆盖，手段是缩短他们在延续护理机构的时间。
The suit, filed this week in the US District Court of Minnesota, was put forward by the estate of two deceased individuals who were denied coverage by UnitedHealth.后果 The plaintiffs argue that the health insurance company should have known how inaccurate its AI was, and that the provider breached its contract by using it.
Their grievances are corroborated by an [investigation from _Stat News_](https://www.statnews.com/2023/11/14/unitedhealth-algorithm-medicare-advantage-investigation/) into UnitedHealth's internal practices at its subsidiary NaviHealth, which found that the company forced employees to unwaveringly adhere to the AI algorithm's questionable projections on how long patients could stay in extended care.
该诉讼于本周在明尼苏达州联邦地方法院提起，由两名生前被联合健康保险拒绝理赔的死者遗产管理方提出。原告辩称，该健康保险公司本应知晓其 AI 的不准确程度，且该提供商因使用该算法而违反了合同。
At least there was a silver lining in the board room: the penny-pinching AI reportedly saved the company an estimated hundreds of millions of dollars it would have been forced to spend on the patients' care otherwise, according to _Stat_.
Though the health claims are rarely appealed, when they are, around 90 percent of them are reversed, according to the lawsuit. That suggests that the AI is egregiously inaccurate, and that by placing undue trust in it, UnitedHealth is scamming countless vulnerable patients out of their healthcare.
《Stat News》对联合健康保险子公司 NaviHealth 内部做法的一项调查证实了他们的不满。调查发现，公司强迫员工坚定不移地遵循 AI 算法关于患者可在延续护理机构停留时长的可疑预测。
"If UnitedHealth is using \\[NaviHealth’s\\] algorithms as gospel... that’s not clinical decision-making," Spencer Perlman, a healthcare markets analyst, told _Stat_. "That’s aggregating data and using an algorithm to make a decision that has nothing to do with the individual themselves."
UnitedHealth fired back in a statement to _Stat_.
至少董事会里还有一线希望：据《Stat》报道，这款吝啬的 AI 据称为公司节省了估计数亿美元，否则这些钱本不得不花在患者的护理上。
"The assertions that NaviHealth uses or incentivizes employees to use a tool to deny care are false," it read. "Adverse coverage decisions are made by medical directors and based on Medicare coverage criteria, not a tool or a performance goal tied to any single quality metric."
Documents and employee testimony seem to corroborate the questionable decisionmaking of UnitedHealth's AI, though.
诉讼称，虽然这些健康理赔很少被上诉，但一旦上诉，约 90% 的拒赔决定会被推翻。这表明该 AI 极不准确，且联合健康保险因对其给予不当信任，正在骗取无数弱势患者的医疗服务。
In one case, the nH Predict system allotted a mere 20 days of rehab for an older woman who was found paralyzed after suffering a stroke — just half the average for impaired stroke patients, according to _Stat_. An elderly, legally blind man with a failing heart and kidneys only received a shockingly inadequate 16 days to recover.
What could be making nH Predict so wrong? It's basing its projections on the length of stays of some six million previous patients in the company's database. On its face, that may appear sound, but that means the AI is inheriting the errors and cost-cutting of those previous decisions — and above all, failing to account for exigent factors both clinical and practical.
“如果联合健康保险将 [NaviHealth 的] 算法奉为圭臬……那就不是临床决策，”医疗市场分析师斯宾塞·帕尔曼告诉《Stat》，“那是聚合数据并利用算法做出与个人本身毫无关系的决定。”
"Length of stay is not some biological variable," Ziad Obermeyer, a physician at University of California, Berkeley, and a researcher of algorithmic bias, told _Stat_.
"People are being forced out of the \\[nursing home\\] because they can't pay or because their insurance sucks," he added. "And so the algorithm is basically learning all the inequalities of our current system."
联合健康保险在给《Stat》的一份声明中进行了反驳。
Yet UnitedHealth would only make its standards more extreme. In 2022, case managers were instructed to keep nursing home stays within three percent of the AI's projection.
Next year, however, it was narrowed to less than one percent, effectively giving employees zero leeway. If case managers failed to hit that target, they were disciplined or fired, according to _Stat_.
“关于 NaviHealth 使用或激励员工使用工具拒绝护理的断言是错误的，”声明写道。“不利的承保决定是由医疗总监做出的，并基于 Medicare 承保标准，而非某种工具或与任何单一质量指标挂钩的绩效目标。”
"By the end of my time at NaviHealth I realized — I'm not an advocate, I'm just a moneymaker for this company," Amber Lynch, a former NaviHealth case manager who was fired earlier this year, told _Stat_. "It's all about money and data points," she added. "It takes the dignity out of the patient, and I hated that."
All told, it sounds like a grim example of how the seeming objectivity of AI can be used to cover up shady practices and exploit people at their most vulnerable.
然而，文件和员工证词似乎证实了联合健康保险 AI 决策的可疑之处。
Document 3160: UnitedHealth Group served class action lawsuit for AI-informed managed care denials
UnitedHealthcare is being sued for allegedly using unreliable artificial intelligence algorithms to wrongfully deny payment for post-acute managed care.风险
联合健康保险公司（UnitedHealthcare）因涉嫌使用不可靠的人工智能算法错误拒绝支付急性期后管理护理费用而被起诉。
The three defendants named [in the complaint](https://fingfx.thomsonreuters.com/gfx/legaldocs/lbvgoerodvq/Lokken%20v%20UnitedHealth%20complaint%2011-14.pdf) filed Tuesday are UnitedHealth Group, its health insurance segment UnitedHealthcare, and its subsidiary technology firm NaviHealth, which created the AI tool at issue called nH Predict.
The complaint alleges that nH Predict has an error rate of 90%, but UHG continues to use it because only a small proportion of policyholders tend to appeal denied claims for service. The rest either pay out-of-pocket for the denied care or forgo the care entirely, it said.
周二提交的[起诉书](https://fingfx.thomsonreuters.com/gfx/legaldocs/lbvgoerodvq/Lokken%20v%20UnitedHealth%20complaint%2011-14.pdf)中点名的三名被告是：联合健康集团（UnitedHealth Group）、其健康保险部门联合健康保险公司，以及其子公司、技术开发公司 NaviHealth，该公司开发了涉事的名为 nH Predict 的 AI 工具。
“Defendants systematically deploy an AI algorithm to prematurely and in bad faith discontinue payment for healthcare services for elderly individuals with serious diseases and injuries,” the complaint noted. “Defendants also utilize the nH Predict AI Model to aggressively deny coverage because they know they will not be held accountable for wrongful denials.风险控制”
Plaintiffs are seeking damages for out-of-pocket costs incurred for post-acute care denied by UHG, emotional distress, attorneys’ fees and demanded a jury trial. They estimated that hundreds of individuals could have been wrongfully denied care because of nH Predict, and more than $5 million is potentially at stake.
起诉书指控称，nH Predict 的错误率高达 90%，但联合健康集团仍继续使用它，因为只有极少数投保人倾向于对被拒绝的服务索赔进行申诉。起诉书指出，其余投保人要么自掏腰包支付被拒护理的费用，要么完全放弃护理。
Some lawmakers have recently drawn attention to Medicare Advantage health insurers’ use of AI applications to deny patients prescribed care. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), for example, [denounced the practice](https://www.mcknightshomecare.com/home-care-providers-applaud-lawmakers-scrutiny-of-ma-plan-prior-authorizations/) during a Senate subcommittee hearing in May.
UHG was also accused of relying on results from nH Predict rather than doctors’ opinions to determine whether post-acute care, such as home health, will be approved or denied. As a result, UHG saved money by reducing the labor costs of paying medical professionals to “conduct an individualized, manual review of each of its insured’s claims.”
起诉书指出：“被告系统性部署 AI 算法，恶意提前终止对患有严重疾病和受伤老年人的医疗服务支付。被告还利用 nH Predict AI 模型激进地拒绝承保，因为他们知道自己不会因错误拒赔而被追责。”
And where UHG saves money, taxpayers lose money, the complaint alleges. Oftentimes, Medicare-eligible UHG policyholders are told that care was denied “solely due to their Medicare eligibility,” and are directed to instead enroll in Medicare to receive services, it said.

Document 1865: Confused self-driving taxi drives away from its support crew
**CHANDLER, Ariz. —** A confused [Waymo](https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/06/tech/waymo-self-driving/index.html) self-driving taxi car was captured on video as it became stranded on an [Arizona](https://www.cnn.com/videos/politics/2021/05/17/election-audit-arizona-reality-check-avlon-newday-vpx.cnn) road [earlier this month](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zdKCQKBvH-A) while carrying a passenger and then unexpectedly driving away as a worker from the company's roadside assistance arrived to help.
**亚利桑那州钱德勒 ——** 一辆不知所措的 Waymo 自动驾驶出租车本月早些时候在亚利桑那州的一条公路上陷入困境，当时车上正载有一名乘客。视频记录下了这一幕：当该公司的一名路边援助人员赶到现场准备提供帮助时，这辆车却意外地开走了。
But the Waymo vehicle soon became stuck farther down the road, which was lined with construction cones. The Waymo worker caught up to the vehicle, took over, and drove the paying passenger to his final destination. Waymo operates a limited ridehail service in Chandler, Arizona.
Autonomous vehicle experts who reviewed the video footage of the 41-minute trip posted on YouTube by the Waymo passenger say it shows a series of gaffes by the Waymo self-driving technology.
但这辆 Waymo 车辆很快就在前方布满施工锥的道路上再次被困。那名 Waymo 工作人员追上了车辆，接管了驾驶，并将这位付费乘客送到了最终目的地。Waymo 在亚利桑那州钱德勒市运营着一项有限的网约车服务。
"The first one was understandable. The second was strange. The third one was jaw-dropping and the fourth one I threw up my hands," Noah Goodall, a University of Virginia scientist who researches vehicle communication and automation, told CNN Business.
First, the Waymo vehicle paused at a stop sign rather than turning onto a street lined with cones. Waymo told CNN Business that guidance provided from one of its employees to revise the car's trajectory was "improper," and declined to elaborate. Waymo has remote workers who can provide information and directions to the self-driving vehicles.风险控制 They can not take manual control of the vehicles.
观看了这位 Waymo 乘客发布在 YouTube 上的长达 41 分钟行程视频的自动驾驶汽车专家表示，视频显示了 Waymo 自动驾驶技术的一系列失误。
The car then completed the turn, but soon stopped in the road, blocking part of a lane of traffic. Construction sites [are known](https://money.cnn.com/2017/06/07/technology/business/maps-wars-self-driving-cars/index.html) to be a challenge for fully autonomous vehicles because they rely on detailed maps of their environment to navigate safely. When the car's environment changes, such as with traffic cones or lane closures, it can struggle to operate at its best.
Following a four-minute stop, it backed up slightly, further blocking a traffic lane. Human motorists had to cross a double yellow line to go around the Waymo vehicle. Some honked.
“第一个失误尚可理解。第二个很奇怪。第三个令人目瞪口呆，到了第四个，我已经无奈地举手投降了，”研究车辆通信和自动化的弗吉尼亚大学科学家诺亚·古德尔告诉 CNN 商业频道。
A construction crew removed a cone in the Waymo vehicle's path, but the car remained stopped.
A few minutes later, the Waymo car pulled away, surprising a Waymo worker who was explaining to the van's passenger, Joel Johnson, through the car's audio system that roadside assistance was on its way. The worker encouraged Johnson to remain seated and keep his seat belt on.
首先，这辆 Waymo 车辆在一个停车标志处停了下来，而不是转弯驶入一条摆满锥桶的街道。Waymo 告诉 CNN 商业频道，其一名员工提供的修正车辆行驶路线的指导是“不当的”，但拒绝详细说明。Waymo 拥有远程工作人员，可以向自动驾驶车辆提供信息和指令。他们无法对车辆进行手动控制。
"Are we moving?" the worker asked in a confused tone.
Further down the road, the Waymo van halted again, amid yet more cones. It was then that a Waymo roadside assistance vehicle arrived.
随后车辆完成了转弯，但很快便停在路中，挡住了部分车道。众所周知，施工现场对全自动驾驶车辆来说是一个挑战，因为它们依赖详细的环境地图来安全导航。当车辆周围的环境发生变化时，例如出现交通锥或车道封闭，车辆就难以发挥最佳运行状态。
Johnson was told by the Waymo worker on the car's audio system that the human driver would take over.
"You better hurry up, it's going to escape," Johnson warned the Waymo worker. Then, as the human driver approached, the Waymo car drove away again, but only a short distance.
在停驶四分钟后，车辆向后倒了一点，进一步阻挡了行车道。人类驾驶员不得不越过双黄线绕过这辆 Waymo 车辆。有些人按响了喇叭。
"I don't even know what's going on anymore," Johnson said in the video.
Johnson told CNN Business that he arrived about 20 minutes late at his destination following the mishaps, and received a Waymo refund.
一名施工人员移除了 Waymo 车辆行进路线上的一个锥桶，但这辆车依然停着不动。
"If you need to really be on time you don't generally take Waymo yet," Johnson told CNN Business in an interview.
Even so, Johnson, who said he's taken 146 trips in Waymo vehicles, said he doesn't think the public should be concerned with the safety of Waymo's self-driving cars, and he continues to ride in the vehicles.
几分钟后，这辆 Waymo 汽车开走了，这让一名 Waymo 工作人员感到惊讶，当时他正通过车载音频系统向车上的乘客乔尔·约翰逊解释路边援助正在路上。该工作人员让约翰逊留在座位上并系好安全带。
"I've seen so much impressive technology," Johnson said of Waymo. "It seems disingenuous to write them off because of one incident."
Waymo said in a statement that the situation was "not ideal," and the self-driving car had received incorrect guidance, which made it challenging for the autonomous vehicle to resume its intended route.
“我们在动吗？”这名工作人员用困惑的语气问道。
Bryant Walker Smith, who studies autonomous vehicles at the University of South Carolina, said he was surprised a command was never issued to halt the Waymo vehicle in place, so roadside assistance could take over.
"There wasn't great coordination among the in-vehicle system, this remote monitoring capacity of the operator on the line and the on-ground assistance," Smith said.
在道路前方，这辆 Waymo 面包车在更多的锥桶中再次停下。直到这时，一辆 Waymo 路边援助车辆才赶到。
Document 1903: Waymo self-driving taxi confused by traffic cones flees help
**A self-driving taxi has blocked a road in Arizona after becoming confused by a lane closed off with traffic cones.**
**一辆自动驾驶出租车在亚利桑那州因被交通锥封闭的车道搞糊涂而阻塞了道路。**
The Waymo vehicle repeatedly drove away from roadside assistance, dispatched within minutes of the car becoming stuck.后果
Passenger Joel Johnson documented the experience [on his YouTube channel.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zdKCQKBvH-A)
这辆Waymo车辆反复驶离道路救援人员，而救援人员是在车辆被困后几分钟内 dispatched 的。
The Alphabet-owned company said it was an "unusual situation" and the taxi had operated safely throughout the journey.
Waymo is the first fully self-driving taxi service legally allowed to operate.
乘客乔尔·约翰逊在他的YouTube频道上记录了这段经历。
For now, it is available in the East Valley district of Phoenix only.
But there are several traffic cones on the right lane of the road, causing it to stop.
这家归Alphabet所有的公司表示，这是一个“不寻常的情况”，且出租车在整个行程中均安全运行。
At this point, the remote-assistance helpline is called and a member of staff speaks to Mr Johnson through the car's system - updating him on when roadside assistance will arrive.
A few minutes later, the taxi moves into an open left lane and then repositions itself so it blocks the road entirely.
Waymo是首个获得合法运营许可的全自动驾驶出租车服务。
Construction workers arrive to remove the cones, giving the taxi a clear path, but it stays still for a few minutes.
Then, when roadside assistance arrives, the taxi starts driving away.
目前，该服务仅在凤凰城的东谷地区提供。
A few moments later, the taxi stops a second time - after being confronted with traffic cones again - and then drives off once more as roadside assistance approaches.
Eventually, the car is disabled and a human driver takes over the wheel.
但道路右侧车道上有几个交通锥，导致车辆停下。
But the specialist team had provided incorrect guidance, the taxi had been unable to complete the trip and roadside assistance had had to step in.
“While the situation was not ideal, the Waymo Driver operated the vehicle safely until roadside assistance arrived," the company said.
此时，远程援助热线被接通，一名工作人员通过车载系统与约翰逊先生通话——告知他道路救援何时到达。
“Throughout, Waymo’s team was in touch with the rider, who provided thoughtful and helpful feedback that allows us to continue learning and improving the Waymo Driver.
“Our team has already assessed the event and improved our operational process.”
几分钟后，出租车驶入畅通的左侧车道，然后调整位置，结果完全堵住了道路。
Mr Johnson regularly posts videos about his experience in Waymo taxis and defended the technology.
"I'm just being honest with what I see," he tweeted.
建筑工人赶到移走了交通锥，为出租车让出了通道，但它仍静止了几分钟。
"How can I prove the technology is great, if I hide it when the occasional mistake happens?
> Speaking as the video maker here, this Waymo performance with cones is the exception to the rule. People are ignoring my other 53 videos where it works just fine.
随后，当道路救援到达时，出租车开始驶离。
>
> — Joel Johnson (@jjricks\\_) [May 14, 2021](https://twitter.com/jjricks_/status/1393211642301714437?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)
片刻之后，出租车第二次停下——因为再次遇到交通锥——然后在道路救援靠近时再次开走。
The BBC is not responsible for the content of external sites.[View original tweet on Twitter](https://twitter.com/jjricks_/status/1393211642301714437)
"This Waymo performance with cones is the exception to the rule.
最终，车辆被停用，由一名人类驾驶员接管方向盘。
“People are ignoring my other 53 videos where it works just fine."

Document 3510: Google suspends Gemini AI chatbot's ability to generate pictures of people
Google said Thursday it is temporarily stopping its Gemini artificial intelligence chatbot from generating images of people a day after apologizing for “inaccuracies” in historical depictions that it was creating.后果
Google周四表示，正在暂时停止其Gemini人工智能聊天机器人生成人物图像的功能。此前一天，该公司曾为其生成的历史画面中的“不准确”之处道歉。
Gemini users this week posted screenshots on social media of historically white-dominated scenes with racially diverse characters that they say it generated, leading critics to raise questions about whether the company is over-correcting for the risk of racial bias in its AI model.
“We’re already working to address recent issues with Gemini’s image generation feature,” Google said in a post on the social media platform X. “While we do this, we’re going to pause the image generation of people and will re-release an improved version soon.”
本周，Gemini用户在社交媒体上发布了历史场景的截图，这些场景原本以白人为主，但他们称Gemini却生成了种族多元化的人物形象。批评者因此质疑该公司是否对人工智能模型中种族偏见风险矫枉过正。
Previous studies have shown AI image-generators can amplify racial and gender stereotypes found in their training data, and without filters are more likely to show lighter-skinned men when asked to generate a person in various contexts.
Google said on Wednesday that it’s “aware that Gemini is offering inaccuracies in some historical image generation depictions” and that it’s “working to improve these kinds of depictions immediately.”
“我们正在处理Gemini图像生成功能近期出现的问题，”Google在社交媒体平台X上发帖称。“在此期间，我们将暂停人物图像生成，并将在近期重新发布改进版本。”
Gemini can generate a “wide range of people,” which the company said is “generally a good thing” because people around the world use the system but it is “missing the mark.”
University of Washington researcher Sourojit Ghosh, who has studied bias in AI image-generators, said he’s in favor of Google pausing the generation of people’s faces but is a “little conflicted about how we got to this outcome.” Contrary to claims of so-called “white erasure” and the premise that Gemini refuses to generate faces of white people — ideas circulating on social media this week — Ghosh’s research has largely found the opposite.
先前的研究表明，人工智能图像生成器可能会放大其训练数据中存在的种族和性别刻板印象，如果不加过滤，在不同情境下生成人物图像时更倾向于展示浅肤色男性。
“The rapidness of this response in the face of a lot of other literature and a lot of other research that has shown traditionally marginalized people being erased by models like this — I find a little difficult to square,” he said.
When the AP asked Gemini to generate pictures of people, or even just a big crowd, it responded by saying it’s “working to improve” the ability to do so. “We expect this feature to return soon and will notify you in release updates when it does,” the chatbot said.
Google周三表示，“我们注意到Gemini在某些历史图像生成描述中出现了不准确之处”，并称正在“立即改进这些描述”。
Ghosh said it’s likely that Google can find a way to filter responses to reflect the historical context of a user’s prompt, but solving the broader harms posed by image-generators built on generations of photos and artwork found on the internet requires more than a technical patch.
“You’re not going to overnight come up with a text-to-image generator that does not cause representational harm,” he said. “They are a reflection of the society in which we live.”
Gemini可以生成“广泛的人物类型”，该公司表示这“通常是件好事”，因为世界各地的用户都在使用该系统，但这“未能达到目标”。
Document 3511: Google pauses Gemini’s ability to generate AI images of people after diversity errors
Google says it’s pausing the ability for its Gemini AI to generate images of people, after the tool was found to be [generating inaccurate historical images](https://www.theverge.com/2024/2/21/24079371/google-ai-gemini-generative-inaccurate-historical). Gemini has been creating diverse images of the US Founding Fathers and Nazi-era German soldiers, in what looked like an attempt to subvert the gender and racial stereotypes found in generative AI.
谷歌表示，在发现其Gemini人工智能工具生成的历史图像存在不准确问题后，将暂停其生成人物图像的功能。Gemini一直在生成美国开国元勋和纳粹时期德国士兵的多样化形象，这看似是为了颠覆生成式人工智能中的性别和种族刻板印象。
“We’re already working to address recent issues with Gemini’s image generation feature,” says Google in a [statement posted on X](https://twitter.com/google_comms/status/1760603321944121506). “While we do this, we’re going to pause the image generation of people and will re-release an improved version soon.”
Google’s decision to pause image generation of people in Gemini comes less than 24 hours after the [company apologized](https://www.theverge.com/2024/2/21/24079371/google-ai-gemini-generative-inaccurate-historical) for the inaccuracies in some historical images its AI model generated. Some Gemini users have been requesting images of historical groups or figures like the Founding Fathers and found non-white AI-generated people in the results. That’s led to conspiracy theories online that Google is intentionally avoiding depicting white people.
谷歌在X平台上发布的一份声明中表示：“我们已经在努力解决Gemini图像生成功能近期出现的问题。在此期间，我们将暂停人物图像的生成，并将在不久后推出改进版本。”
_The Verge_ tested several Gemini queries yesterday, which included a request for “a US senator from the 1800s” that returned results that included what appeared to be Black and Native American women. The first female senator was a white woman in 1922, so Gemini’s AI images were essentially erasing the history of race and gender discrimination.
Now that Google has disabled Gemini’s ability to generate pictures of people, here’s how the AI model responds if you request an image of a person:
谷歌决定暂停Gemini的人物图像生成功能，距该公司为其人工智能模型生成的部分历史图像中的不准确问题道歉不到24小时。一些Gemini用户一直在请求生成开国元勋等历史群体或人物的形象，却发现结果中出现了非白人的人工智能生成人物。这引发了一些网络阴谋论，指责谷歌故意避免描绘白人。

Document 3514: Google CEO Sundar Pichai says Gemini chatbot’s ‘woke’ AI disaster ‘completely unacceptable’
Google CEO Sundar Pichai blasted the [Gemini AI chatbot’s widely panned habit of generating “woke” versions](https://nypost.com/2024/02/21/business/googles-ai-chatbot-gemini-makes-diverse-images-of-founding-fathers-popes-and-vikings-so-woke-its-unusable/) of historical figures as “completely unacceptable” in a scathing email to company employees.
谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊在一封措辞严厉的内部邮件中，将Gemini人工智能聊天机器人生成“觉醒”版本历史人物的普遍做法斥为“完全不可接受”。
Pichai said Google’s AI teams are “working around the clock” to fix Gemini – [which was disabled last week](https://nypost.com/2024/02/22/business/google-pauses-absurdly-woke-gemini-ai-chatbots-image-tool-after-backlash-over-historically-inaccurate-pictures/) after the “absurdly woke” chatbot ignited a social media firestorm with bizarrely revisionist pictures such as Black Vikings, female popes, and even “diverse” Nazi-era German soldiers.
“I know that some of its responses have offended our users and shown bias – to be clear, that’s completely unacceptable and we got it wrong,” Pichai said in the Tuesday memo first obtained by [Semafor](https://www.semafor.com/article/02/27/2024/google-ceo-sundar-pichai-calls-ai-tools-responses-completely-unacceptable).
皮查伊表示，谷歌的人工智能团队正在“夜以继日”地修复Gemini——该聊天机器人上周被禁用，此前这个“极其觉醒”的聊天机器人因生成黑人维京人、女性教皇甚至是“多元化”的纳粹时期德国士兵等离谱的篡改历史图片而在社交媒体上引发轩然大波。
The missive marked Pichai’s first public remarks on the PR nightmare [that erased more than $70 billion in market value](https://nypost.com/2024/02/27/business/google-parent-loses-70b-in-market-value-after-woke-ai-chatbot-disaster/) in a single day earlier this week – and raised renewed concerns among critics who say Google’s employees are injecting their political bias into the technology.
Pichai added that Google was “already seeing a substantial improvement on a wide range of prompts.”
“我知道它的一些回应冒犯了我们的用户并显示出偏见——需要明确的是，这是完全不可接受的，我们做错了，”皮查伊在这份周二发布的备忘录中表示，该备忘录最先由Semafor获取。
[](https://nypost.com/2024/02/27/business/googles-700m-play-store-settlement-is-bad-for-consumers-judge/)
“No AI is perfect, especially at this emerging stage of the industry’s development, but we know the bar is high for us and we will keep at it for however long it takes,” Pichai said. “And we’ll review what happened and make sure we fix it at scale.”
这封致歉信标志着皮查伊首次就这场公关噩梦公开发表评论——本周早些时候，该事件在一天之内蒸发了超过700亿美元的市值，并引发了批评者新的担忧，他们认为谷歌员工正在将政治偏见注入技术中。
Gemini’s “woke” image disaster further damaged public trust in Google’s AI tools at a pivotal point for the company, which had just rebranded its chatbot and unveiled the image generation tool a few days earlier.
Google Gemini generated controversy by producing ahistorical images in response to user prompts. Google Gemini
皮查伊补充说，谷歌“在广泛的提示范围内已经看到了实质性改善”。
Concerns about potential bias in Gemini’s model training were exacerbated after social media users resurfaced a set of [politically charged tweets by Google Gemini’s product lead Jack Krawczyk](https://nypost.com/2024/02/22/business/white-privilege-is-f-king-real-google-gemini-product-leads-old-tweets-allegedly-resurface-amid-woke-ai-image-fiasco/). In the old posts, Krawczyk allegedly stated that “white privilege is f—king real” and America is rife with “egregious racism.”
Scrutiny wasn’t limited to Gemini’s image outputs. The chatbot generated further outrage with its text responses after it [refused to condemn pedophilia](https://nypost.com/2024/02/23/business/woke-google-gemini-refuses-to-say-pedophilia-is-wrong-after-diverse-historical-images-debacle-individuals-cannot-control-who-they-are-attracted-to/) and claimed there [was “no right or wrong answer”](https://nypost.com/2024/02/25/us-news/nate-silver-calls-to-shut-down-gemini-after-googles-ai-chatbot-refuses-to-say-if-hitler-or-musk-is-worse/) when asked if Adolf Hitler or Elon Musk is worse.
“没有任何人工智能是完美的，尤其是在行业发展这一新兴阶段，但我们知道对我们的要求很高，我们将继续努力，无论需要多长时间，”皮查伊说。“我们将审查所发生的事情，并确保在大规模范围内修复它。”
The Google boss said the company would take “a clear set of actions” in response to the crisis, including unspecified “structural changes, updated product guidelines, improved launch processes, robust evals and red-teaming, and technical recommendations.”
The problem is expected to take “a few weeks” to fix, one of Google’s top AI executives said at an event earlier this week.
Gemini的“觉醒”图像灾难在这个关键时刻进一步损害了公众对谷歌人工智能工具的信任，该公司几天前刚刚重新命名了其聊天机器人并推出了图像生成工具。
Document 3553: Google AI’s answer on whether Modi is ‘fascist’ sparks outrage in India, calls for tough laws
Tech giant Google is facing a barrage of criticism by followers of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi over responses by its Gemini artificial intelligence (AI) tool that have been perceived as “biased”, prompting calls for tough regulation against the new technology’s downsides.影响
科技巨头谷歌正面临印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪追随者的猛烈批评，起因是其Gemini人工智能工具的回复被认为存在“偏见”，这促使人们呼吁对新技术的负面影响进行严格监管。
The controversy was sparked by a viral post on X, formerly known as Twitter, by journalist Arnab Ray, who posted screenshots of the chatbot’s response to “Is Modi a fascist?” Gemini replied that Modi was “accused of implementing policies some experts have characterised as fascist”.
His screenshots show the same question based on the names of former US President Donald Trump and Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky but did not produce similar answers from Gemini.
这场争议由记者阿纳布·雷在X平台（前身为推特）上发布的一条病毒式传播的帖子引发，他发布了聊天机器人对“莫迪是法西斯主义者吗？”这一问题的回复截图。Gemini回复称莫迪“被指控实施了一些专家定性为法西斯主义的政策”。
A Google spokesperson said in a Hindu Businessline report on Saturday, “We’ve worked quickly to address this issue.
“Gemini is built as a creativity and productivity tool and may not always be reliable, especially when it comes to responding to some prompts about current events, political topics, or evolving news. This is something that we’re constantly working on improving.”
他的截图显示，当用美国前总统唐纳德·特朗普和乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的名字提出同样的问题时，Gemini并没有给出类似的回复。
India’s Minister of Information Technology and Electronics Rajeev Chandrasekhar said the incident violated Indian laws.
“These are direct violations of Rule 3(1)(b) of Intermediary Rules (IT rules) of the IT Act and violations of several provisions of the Criminal Code,” he wrote on social media.
谷歌一位发言人在周六的《印度商业热线》报告中表示：“我们已迅速采取行动解决这个问题。
The minister’s remark prompted calls for India to tighten its rules and regulations to prevent a recurrence of such incidents.
“Heavy intervention is needed by the ministry. Must be told in plain words that access to the Indian market is based on rule of law. Follow the rules or ship out,” Suchit Ahuja, an assistant professor at Concordia University, wrote in response to Chandrasekhar’s report on LinkedIn.
“Gemini是作为创意和生产力工具构建的，可能并不总是可靠的，特别是在回应有关时事、政治话题或不断发展的新闻的某些提示时。这是我们不断努力改进的方面。”
“We do not want an electronic version of the East India Company (EIC) in the 21st century.”
He was referring to the dominant trading company set up by the British Empire to trade popular items such as cotton, silk, tea and opium from its base in India between 1785 and 1858.
印度信息技术和电子部长拉吉夫·钱德拉塞卡尔表示，这一事件违反了印度法律。
To many people in India, the EIC had exploited the riches and labour of the subcontinent, ruined its economy through heavy taxation and used armed force to suppress Indian states.
A responsible approach to AI is needed to ensure human biases are not coded into the training of the algorithms, otherwise, they would become more blatant in responses generated by the technology, Ahuja said.
他在社交媒体上写道：“这些直接违反了《信息技术法》《中介机构规则》第3(1)(b)条以及《刑法典》的多项规定。”
“The fact that such a high-profile leader of a democratic country, who enjoys a 77 per cent approval rating – the highest globally, is being called a fascist in an AI response, is deeply concerning. This reflects poorly on the process of training and design of the AI algorithms,” he added.
**India’s technology laws**
部长的言论引发了人们呼吁印度收紧法规以防止此类事件再次发生。
India introduced stringent new rules to govern social media firms a few years ago under its Information Technology Rules that put platforms such as X and Facebook under greater scrutiny.
Social media companies with more than 5 million users are required to appoint tech compliance officers.
康考迪亚大学助理教授苏奇特·阿胡贾在领英上回应钱德拉塞卡尔的报告时写道：“该部需要大力干预。必须明确告知，進入印度市场是基于法治的。遵守规则或者离开。”
The main role of these officers is to remove content deemed “objectionable” by law enforcement agencies. Companies can challenge these requests in court. Under the law, platforms need to remove sexual content within 24 hours, while they have 15 days to do so for non-sexual offensive content.
But often companies have only complied with the rules half-heartedly so far and the legal system needs an overhaul in this area, lawyers say.
“我们不希望21世纪出现东印度公司（EIC）的电子版本。”
Siddharth Mahajan, a partner at Athena Legal, a New Delhi law firm, said that guidelines for intermediaries under India’s Information Technology Act require them to remove miscommunication or misleading information even if it is AI-generated.
“Otherwise their intermediary status may be revoked,” he said.
他指的是这家主导性贸易公司，由大英帝国于1785年至1858年间在印度设立基地，用于交易棉花、丝绸、茶叶和鸦片等热门商品。
The Indian government says it wants a light touch on regulation on AI “so that innovation is not stifled” but Mahajan said that authorities can take action against Google on the grounds of spreading false information.
Satya Gupta, President of VLSI Society and a veteran of India’s electronics and digital industry, said that generative AI is not meant to give factual information but if the output of such a tool is used incorrectly, it becomes the relevant company’s responsibility.
对许多印度人来说，东印度公司曾掠夺次大陆的财富和劳动力，通过重税摧毁了其经济，并使用武力镇压印度各邦。
**‘Broad approach needed’**
Technology experts said it would be tough for the government to tackle issues involving AI only by updating the law.
阿胡贾表示，需要以负责任的方式发展人工智能，以确保人类偏见不会被编入算法的训练中，否则这些偏见会在技术生成的回复中变得更加明显。
“We have so many laws in India but how many are implemented? Since AI is an emerging technology, you need to keep evolving. [But] technology changes by the hour and laws are not so easy to change,” said Sanjay Kaushik, managing director of security and risk management consultancy Netrika Consulting India Private Ltd.
Kaushik said that AI technology relies on past experiences or data that has been fed to pick out answers to questions. “If somebody in the US feeds the wrong data, then it will provide the answers accordingly,” he said.
他补充道：“一个民主国家如此高调的领导人——拥有77%的支持率，是全球最高的——在人工智能回复中被称为法西斯主义者，这令人深感担忧。这反映出人工智能算法训练和设计过程存在严重问题。”
“It is very difficult to make it independent and unbiased until you can put in algorithms that are totally independent,” he said, adding that Indian authorities can emulate their counterparts in the US and Europe by imposing heavy penalties as a deterrent.
China became the first country last August to introduce a law targeting generative AI – one of several regulations it had passed to curb the spread of different forms of harmful AI.
**印度的技术法律**
In most countries, however, such regulations have not been introduced or are in the pipeline.
The Indian government has proposed to pass legislation called the Digital India Act, which would replace the existing Information Technology Act. But discussions over the matter are still in their early stage and it is unclear what the Act would cover.
印度几年前根据《信息技术规则》引入了严格的社交媒体公司监管新规，使X和Facebook等平台受到更严格的审查。
Analysts say that regulations targeting the harmful side of AI have to be broad in scope as the technology could have a much bigger impact than social media or even the internet.
“India already has laws about the hosting of data, perhaps this is an opportune moment to also devise certain AI-focused laws that provide the necessary deterrents for these types of issues from propagating,” Ahuja said.
拥有超过500万用户的社交媒体公司必须任命技术合规官员。
The Indian government could provide incentives to develop local-specific AI solutions as these could serve as a “mitigation mechanism” and compete with those from the international tech giants, he said.
Document 3567: Google Stops Gemini AI From Making Images Of People—After Musk Calls Service ‘Woke’
Google announced Thursday that it will “pause” its Gemini image generator’s ability to create images of people, after the program was criticized for showing misleading images of people's races in historical contexts—leading billionaire Elon Musk to call the service "woke."风险
谷歌周四宣布将“暂停”其Gemini图像生成器创建人物图片的功能，此前该程序因在历史背景下展示误导性的人物种族图像而受到批评——这导致亿万富翁埃隆·马斯克称该服务“觉醒”。
### Key Facts
Google said Wednesday it was “working to improve these kinds of depictions immediately,” but the company disabled images of people less than 24 hours later, promising an “improved version” of the service soon.
### 关键事实
Google has not provided a timeframe for when image generation of people would return, and has not returned a request for comment from Forbes.
Jack Krawczyk, Google’s product director for Gemini Experiences, confirmed in a [post on X](https://twitter.com/JackK/status/1760334258722250785?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E1760334258722250785%7Ctwgr%5Eaf69b311709239e2936b5a9f24fc95bbcd17a959%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cnbc.com%2F2024%2F02%2F22%2Fgoogle-pauses-gemini-ai-image-generator-after-inaccuracies.html) the chatbot was “offering inaccuracies in some historical image generation depictions,” and said the company was working to “further tune” the service to accurately reflect historical contexts.
谷歌周三表示正在“立即努力改进这些描绘”，但公司不到24小时后就禁用了人物图片，并承诺很快将推出“改进版本”。
Forbes could still use Gemini to create images of inanimate objects such as houses, but could not generate images of people—with the chatbot stating “we expect this feature to return soon and will notify you in release updates when it does.”
Google launched Gemini, a chatbot formerly known as Bard and powered by a large language model, on February 8—competing with generative AI programs like OpenAI’s ChatGPT, which is backed by rival Microsoft. As part of the new service, Gemini offers an image generator, similar to Midjourney and OpenAI’s DALL-E. However, days after release, users began noticing the generator would create images of “historical” figures and scenes with historical inaccuracies. In some examples created by [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/2024/2/21/24079371/google-ai-gemini-generative-inaccurate-historical), the generator displayed images of black women for the prompt “US senator from the 1800s” (the first black woman to serve in the Senate was Carol Moseley Braun, who was elected in 1992). Another image showed women and black men wearing World War II-era German military uniforms. Google has since acknowledged the misleading images. “Gemini’s AI image generation does generate a wide range of people. And that’s generally a good thing because people around the world use it. But it’s missing the mark here,” Google said in a statement posted on X on Wednesday.
谷歌尚未提供人物图像生成恢复的时间表，也未回应福布斯的置评请求。
### Chief Critic
Musk, billionaire founder of competitor xAI, voiced his criticism of Gemini’s image generation service in a [post Tuesday](https://twitter.com/elonmusk/status/1760516729783148583), claiming Google’s AI chatbot was “woke” and “racist.” xAI, on the other hand, is described as maximum truth seeking. The company, which was founded in March 2023, released its chatbot Grok in November, and does not offer image generation services yet.
谷歌Gemini体验产品总监杰克·克劳维克克在一篇X帖子中确认，该聊天机器人“在一些历史图像生成描绘中出现了不准确”，并表示公司正在努力“进一步调整”服务以准确反映历史背景。
Other AI image generators have faced the opposite criticism, frequently being accused of creating racially biased images that disproportionately show white people. A 2023 report in the [Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/interactive/2023/ai-generated-images-bias-racism-sexism-stereotypes/) found these biases were rampant in images generated by Stable Diffusion XL, the service offered by startup Stability AI. Using the service, prompts for “a productive person” and “attractive people” produced images only of white people. Meanwhile, the prompt “person at social services” produced only images of people of color. According to Krawczyk, Google designed Gemini’s image generation to specifically address these problems. “We design our image generation capabilities to reflect our global user base, and we take representation and bias seriously,” the developer said in a [post on Tuesday](https://twitter.com/JackK/status/1760334258722250785?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E1760334258722250785%7Ctwgr%5Eaf69b311709239e2936b5a9f24fc95bbcd17a959%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cnbc.com%2F2024%2F02%2F22%2Fgoogle-pauses-gemini-ai-image-generator-after-inaccuracies.html). “We will continue to do this for open ended prompts (images of a person walking a dog are universal!)”

Document 3770: A national network of local news sites is publishing AI-written articles under fake bylines. Experts are raising alarm
The articles on a local news site popping up around the country appear to cover what any community outlet would focus on: crime, local politics, weather and happenings. "In-depth reporting about your home area," the outlet's slogan proudly declares.
一家在全国各地涌现的本地新闻网站上，其文章似乎涵盖了任何社区媒体都会关注的内容：犯罪、本地政治、天气和时事动态。“深入报道您的家乡，”该媒体的口号自豪地宣称。
But a closer look at the bylines populating the local site and a national network of others --- Sarah Kim, Jake Rodriguez, Mitch M. Rosenthal --- reveals a tiny badge with the words "AI." These are not real bylines. In fact, the names don't even belong to real humans. The articles were written with the use of artificial intelligence.
The outlet, Hoodline, is not the first or only news site to harness AI. News organizations across the world are grappling with how to take advantage of the rapidly developing technology, while also not being overrun by it.
但如果仔细观察这家本地网站以及全国性网络中其他网站文章的署名——莎拉·金、杰克·罗德里格斯、米奇·M·罗森塔尔——就会发现一个带有“AI”字样的小徽章。这些并非真实的署名。事实上，这些名字甚至不属于真正的人类。这些文章是借助人工智能撰写的。
But experts warn that relying too heavily on AI could wreck the credibility of news organizations and potentially supercharge the spread of misinformation if not kept in close check. Media companies integrating AI in news publishing have also seen it backfire, resulting in public embarrassments. Tech outlet CNET's AI-generated articles made embarrassing factual errors. The nation's largest newspaper chain owner, Gannett, pulled back on an AI experiment reporting on high school sports games after public mockery. Sports Illustrated deleted several articles from its website after they were found to have been published under fake author names.
Hoodline, founded in 2014 as a San Francisco-based hyper-local news outlet with a mission "to cover the news deserts that no one else is covering," once employed a newsroom full of human journalists. The outlet has since expanded into a national network of local websites, covering news and events in major cities across the country and drawing millions of readers each month, the company said.
该媒体 Hoodline 并非第一个也不是唯一一个利用 AI 的新闻网站。世界各地的新闻机构都在努力探索如何利用这一迅速发展的技术，同时又不被其吞噬。
But last year, Hoodline began filling its site with AI-generated articles. A disclaimer page linked at the bottom of its pages notes to readers, "While AI may assist in the background, the essence of our journalism --- from conception to publication --- is driven by real human insight and discretion."
Zachary Chen, chief executive of Hoodline parent company Impress3, which acquired the site in 2020, defended the site's use of AI and its transparency with readers, telling CNN the outlet provides valuable reporting in news deserts around the country and is generating revenue to hire more human journalists in the future.
但专家警告称，如果不受严格监管，过度依赖 AI 可能会破坏新闻机构的公信力，并可能极大地助长虚假信息的传播。将 AI 整合到新闻发布中的媒体公司也已遭遇反噬，导致公开出丑。科技媒体 CNET 的 AI 生成文章犯了令人尴尬的事实性错误。美国最大的报业连锁集团所有者甘尼特在遭到公众嘲讽后，停止了一项报道高中体育比赛的 AI 实验。《体育画报》在被发现使用假作者姓名发布文章后，删除了其网站上的几篇文章。
Hoodline's staff includes "dozens of editors, as well as dozens of journalist researchers, full time," Chen said. The outlet also employs a "growing number of on-the-ground journalists who research and write original stories about their neighborhood beats," he added, referencing recent articles about restaurants, retail stores and events in the San Francisco area.
Bios for bots
Hoodline 成立于 2014 年，是一家总部位于旧金山的超本地新闻媒体，其使命是“报道其他人未涉及的新闻荒漠”，曾经拥有一个满是人类记者的编辑部。该公司表示，该媒体此后已扩展为一个全国性的本地网站网络，报道全国主要城市的新闻和事件，每月吸引数百万读者。

But until recently, the site had further blurred the line between reality and illusion. Screenshots captured last year by the Internet Archive and local outlet Gazetteer showed Hoodline had further embellished its AI author bylines with what appeared to be AI-generated headshots resembling real people and fake biographical information.
但去年，Hoodline 开始在其网站上填充 AI 生成的文章。其页面底部链接的一份免责声明提醒读者：“虽然 AI 可能在后台提供协助，但我们新闻业的精髓——从构思到发布——是由真正的人类洞察力和判断力驱动的。”
"Nina is a long-time writer and a Bay Area Native who writes about good food & delicious drink, tantalizing tech & bustling business," one biography claimed.
The fake headshots and biographies have since been removed from the site, replaced with a small "AI" badge next to each machine-assisted article's byline, though they still carry human names. The archived screenshots have also been wiped from much of the internet. Wayback Machine director Mark Graham told CNN that archived pages of Hoodline's AI writers were removed last month "at the request of the rights holder of the site."
Hoodline 母公司 Impress3 的首席执行官扎卡里·陈于 2020 年收购了该网站，他为该网站使用 AI 及其对读者的透明度进行了辩护。他告诉 CNN，该媒体为全国各地的新闻荒漠提供了有价值的报道，并且正在创造收入，以便在未来雇佣更多人类记者。
Chen acknowledged the company requested that the archive's screenshots of the site be removed from the internet, saying "some websites have taken outdated screenshots from months or even years ago to mischaracterize our present-day practices."

But experts expressed alarm over Hoodline's practices, warning that it exemplifies the potential pitfalls and perils of using AI in journalism, threatening to diminish public trust in news.
机器人的简介
The way the site uses and discloses AI purposely tricks readers by "mimicking" the look and feel of a "standards-based local news organization with real journalists," said Peter Adams, a senior vice president of the News Literacy Project, which aims to educate the public on identifying credible information.
"It's a kind of flagrantly opaque way to dupe people into thinking that they're reading actual reporting by an actual journalist who has a concern for being fair, for being accurate, for being transparent," Adams told CNN.
但直到最近，该网站还在进一步模糊现实与幻象的界限。互联网档案馆和当地媒体《公报》去年捕获的屏幕截图显示，Hoodline 进一步修饰了其 AI 作者署名，配上了看似真人的 AI 生成头像和虚假的传记信息。

Chen would not disclose what AI system Hoodline is employing, only calling it "our own proprietary and custom-built software, combined with the most cutting-edge AI partners to craft publish-ready, fact-based article." Each article, Chen said, is overseen by editors before it is published.
“尼娜是一位长期撰稿人，也是湾区土生土长的当地人，撰写关于美食佳酿、诱人科技和繁忙商业的文章，”其中一份传记声称。

The News/Media Alliance, which represents more than 2,200 US publishers, has supported news organizations taking legal action against AI developers who are harvesting news content without permission. Danielle Coffey, the group's chief executive, told CNN that Hoodline's content "is likely a violation of copyright law."
这些虚假头像和传记已从网站上移除，取而代之的是每篇机器辅助文章署名旁的一个小“AI”徽章，尽管它们仍然使用人类的名字。存档的屏幕截图也已从互联网的大部分地方被清除。Wayback Machine（回溯机器）主管马克·格雷厄姆告诉 CNN，Hoodline AI 作者的存档页面已于上个月“应网站权利持有人的要求”被移除。
"It's another example of stealing our content without permission and without compensation to then turn around and compete with the original work," Coffey said. "Without quality news in the first place, this type of content among other practices will become unsustainable over time, as quality news will simply disappear."
Chen told CNN he takes copyright law very seriously and that the outlet has "greatly refined processes with heavy guardrails." The site's readers, he asserted, "appreciate the unbiased nature of our AI-assisted news," and claimed Hoodline's visitor traffic has soared twentyfold since the publication was acquired. (Chen did not specify their traffic numbers.)
陈承认公司要求移除互联网上该网站的存档屏幕截图，称“一些网站利用几个月甚至几年前的过时屏幕截图，歪曲了我们目前的做法。”
That's not to say there isn't a place for AI in a newsroom. “一种空洞的透明姿态”

Research conducted by Simon and Benjamin Toff, a journalism professor at the University of Minnesota, has also found that the public has not embraced the use of AI in news reporting.
但专家对 Hoodline 的做法表示担忧，警告称这体现了在新闻业使用 AI 的潜在陷阱和危险，有可能削弱公众对新闻的信任。
"We found that people are somewhat less trusting of news labelled as AI, and there is reason to believe that people won't be as willing to pay for news generated purely with AI," he said.

Document 3976: AI-Powered News Site Accidentally Accuses District Attorney of Murder
A controversial AI-powered local news site really stepped in it this week — by accidentally accusing a regional district attorney of murder.
一家备受争议的AI驱动本地新闻网站本周真是闯了大祸——它意外地指控一名地区检察官犯有谋杀罪。
As [_Techdirt_ first reported](https://www.techdirt.com/2024/10/15/ai-sludge-local-news-site-hoodline-falsely-accuses-san-mateo-da-of-murder/), an [article appeared](https://archive.fo/RBB1Q) on _Hoodline San Jose_ — one of the media network's many local news sites that span the US — earlier this month with a gruesome headline: "SAN MATEO COUNTY DA CHARGED WITH MURDER AMID ONGOING SEARCH FOR VICTIM'S REMAINS."
That's bleak stuff, not to mention a crime that probably would have made national news. But there's an important reason why it _didn't_ hit national airwaves: there was a murder, but the DA didn't commit it. They just charged the guy who allegedly did.
据《Techdirt》率先报道，本月初，《Hoodline San Jose》——该媒体网络遍布美国的众多本地新闻网站之一——刊登了一篇文章，标题耸人听闻：“圣马特奥县地方检察官被控谋杀，目前正在搜寻受害者遗骸。”
As _Techdirt_ found, _Hoodline_'s AI seems to have taken an X-formerly-Twitter post from the San Mateo DA office's official account, in which the office shared a run-of-the-mill press release about a local man — who was _not_ the DA — finally being charged _by the DA's office_ for the awful crime and garbled it so badly that it said the DA himself committed the grisly murder. We're all [innocent](https://futurism.com/the-byte/ai-accuses-journalist-crimes) [until](https://futurism.com/crime-fighting-ai-jail-little-evidence) [accused by AI](https://futurism.com/the-byte/elon-musk-ai-accuses-nba-player-criminal-vandalism) [of crimes](https://futurism.com/the-byte/openai-chatgpt-accuses-crimes).
After _Techdirt_ called _Hoodline_ out for the cataclysmic error, a word soup of an [editor's note](https://hoodline.com/2024/10/san-mateo-county-da-charged-with-murder-amid-ongoing-search-for-victim-s-remains/) appeared at the top of the article. It attributed the flub to a simple "typo" that "unfortunately changed the meaning" of its content, "thereby creating ambiguity about the fact that the DA and the accused are two different people."
这听起来令人毛骨悚然，更不用说这种罪行本该成为全国头条新闻。但这之所以没有登上全国新闻频道，有一个重要原因：确实发生了谋杀案，但不是地方检察官干的。检察官只是对涉嫌作案的人提起了指控。
Mistakes happen in journalism. But as far as journalistic errors go, boldly accusing the wrong person of murder — let alone levying such an accusation at a high-ranking local official — is _pretty_ high up there in terms of seriousness.
Add that _Hoodline_, which is currently owned by a murky media outfit called Impress3, is openly using AI to find and cough up synthetic "news," and it's the latest [significant blunder](https://futurism.com/cnet-ai-errors) by a media organization or a paid third-party provider attempting to [use AI](https://futurism.com/gannett-promised-responsible-ai-bungling) to cheaply [churn out content](https://futurism.com/sports-illustrated-ai-generated-writers).
正如《Techdirt》所发现的，《Hoodline》的AI似乎提取了圣马特奥地检官办公室官方账号在X（前推特）上发布的一篇帖子。该办公室在帖子中分享了一份关于一名当地男子的例行新闻稿——此人并非地检官——内容是地检官办公室终于起诉了这名犯下可怕罪行的男子。然而，AI将信息严重扭曲，竟称地检官本人犯下了这起残忍的谋杀案。我们本都坚信“在被证明有罪前是无辜的”，除非被AI指控犯罪。
The error also calls into question _Hoodline_'s florid promises that its editorial content is crafted with a meaningful level of human oversight.
"We view journalism as a creative science and an art that necessitates a human touch," [reads](https://hoodline.com/disclaimer/) the company's AI disclaimer. "In our pursuit of delivering informative and captivating content, we integrate artificial intelligence (AI) to support and enhance our editorial processes."
在《Techdirt》揭露了《Hoodline》这一灾难性的错误后，文章顶部出现了一段措辞混乱的“编辑说明”。该说明将这一失误归咎于一个简单的“拼写错误”，称其“不幸地改变了内容含义，从而导致了关于地检官和被告是两个不同的人这一事实的模糊。”
The article was attributed to the byline Eileen Vargas, one of the website's many fake, AI-generated reporter personas. As [_Nieman Lab_ reported](https://futurism.com/ai-fake-racially-diverse-writers) earlier this year, _Hoodline_'s vast lineup of made-up journalists has drawn wide scrutiny for feigning racial diversity in an industry that, in reality, is overwhelmingly white and male.
There might be some implications for Google — an AI company [reportedly testing AI news products](https://futurism.com/google-paying-journalists-articles-ai) itself — as well. According to _Techdirt_'s Mike Masnick, he discovered the false AI accusation when the _Hoodline_ piece cropped up in his Google News tab. And again, though journalists make mistakes, Google's algorithm platforming erroneous accusations of murder put forth by an explicitly AI-powered news network raises a different set of eyebrows.
新闻行业难免出错。但就新闻错误而言，公然指控错人犯有谋杀罪——更不用说还是指控一位级别较高的地方官员——其严重程度可谓登峰造极。
How much leash should an AI news site with clearly low editorial standards be given? And can we trust news-sorting algorithms to sift through the rising tide of algorithm-generated content?
What we can say for sure is this: mistakes like these, which a human reporter working under a sound editorial process would be very unlikely to make, are likely to become more and more common as publishers give control over to cheap and barely-supervised AI systems.
再加上《Hoodline》目前由一家名为Impress3的不透明媒体机构拥有，并且公开使用AI来挖掘并炮制合成的“新闻”，这已成为媒体机构或付费第三方供应商试图利用AI廉价批量生产内容的最新一起重大失误。

There might be some implications for Google — an AI company reportedly testing AI news products itself — as well. According to Techdirt's Mike Masnick, he discovered the false AI accusation when the Hoodline piece cropped up in his Google News tab. And again, though journalists make mistakes, Google's algorithm platforming erroneous accusations of murder put forth by an explicitly AI-powered news network raises a different set of eyebrows.后果
新闻业难免出错。但在新闻错误中，公然指控错误对象犯有谋杀罪——更不用说还是针对一位地方高官——其严重程度可谓极高。
How much leash should an AI news site with clearly low editorial standards be given? And can we trust news-sorting algorithms to sift through the rising tide of algorithm-generated content?
What we can say for sure is this: mistakes like these, which a human reporter working under a sound editorial process would be very unlikely to make, are likely to become more and more common as publishers give control over to cheap and barely-supervised AI systems.
